overview: Mali is a large landlocked country in West Africa. Its capital and largest city is Bamako. In the past it was the centre of great empires, including the Mali Empire, whose ruler Mansa Musa is often said to be one of the richest people in history, and Timbuktu was a famous centre of learning. Mali became independent from France in 1960.

geography.text: The north of Mali lies in the Sahara Desert, the centre is the dry Sahel, and the south is savanna. The Niger river curves through the country and forms a large inland delta that floods every year, supporting farming and fishing.

history.text: Mali was the heart of great empires. The Mali Empire's ruler Mansa Musa made a famous pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324 with so much gold that he became known as one of the richest people in history. Timbuktu became a centre of learning. France colonised the region in the late 1800s, and Mali became independent in 1960. Conflict in the north began in 2012.

events.title: Mali Empire
events.text: Sundiata Keita founds the Mali Empire.

events.title: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage
events.text: Mali's ruler travels to Mecca with vast amounts of gold.

events.title: Songhai falls
events.text: A Moroccan army defeats the Songhai Empire.

events.title: Northern conflict
events.text: Rebels and armed groups take the north.

government.text: Mali has been ruled by the military since coups in 2020 and 2021. The junta has delayed elections and dissolved political parties in 2025. Together with Burkina Faso and Niger, it left ECOWAS to form the Alliance of Sahel States. Armed groups control parts of the north and centre.

economy.text: Gold is Mali's main export, along with cotton. Most people work in farming and herding along the Niger River.

culture.text: Mali has a rich musical tradition, from griots who sing family histories to desert blues bands and stars such as Salif Keita and Amadou & Mariam. Timbuktu's ancient manuscripts and the Great Mosque of Djenné, the world's largest mud-brick building, are UNESCO sites.

items.title: Great Mosque of Djenné
items.text: Rebuilt in mud every year by the community.

items.title: Timbuktu manuscripts
items.text: Hundreds of thousands of historic texts.

items.title: Kora
items.text: Played by griots across the Mande world.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport, and Mali reached the Africa Cup of Nations final in 1972. Basketball is also strong, especially for women.

items.title: Seydou Keita
items.text: Won the Champions League with Barcelona.

didYouKnow: The Great Mosque of Djenné is the largest mud-brick building in the world.
Mansa Musa of Mali is often called one of the richest people in history.

keyPeople.name: Mansa Musa
keyPeople.text: Ruled the Mali Empire in the 1300s.
